column5: 位 is polite. To say how many people are in a family, use 口: 我家有三口人.
名 is used in formal counts, as in a news report or a school notice.
位 shows respect, so it is the usual choice in polite speech.
份 is one copy of the paper; 张 is a single sheet.
部 counts films as works. For one showing at the cinema, use 场: 一场电影.
艘 is used for larger ships and in formal writing.
件 is one item of clothing; 套 is a whole outfit.
双 is a pair of shoes; 只 is one shoe.
只 is one hand; 双 is both hands.
只 is one eye; 双 is both eyes.
根 counts single hairs.
朵 is one flower; 束 is a bunch.
套 is a flat or home you live in; 座 is a whole building.
把 is one key; 串 is a bunch of keys.
个 is a whole melon; 块 is a slice.
串 is a whole bunch.
串 is a bunch; 颗 is one grape.
块 is a slice; 个 is a whole cake.
片 is a slice; 个 is a loaf or roll.
道 is used for dishes served in a meal, as on a menu.
片 is one tablet.
Yes, 床 (bed) is also a measure word here.
道 is used for questions on a test.
节 is one class period; 门 is a whole course.
场 is a spell of rain; 阵 is a short shower.
笔 is a sum of money. 块 and 元 are units of money, not measure words for 钱: 十块钱.
Without 个, 一月 means January.
No measure word: 一天, 三天. 天 works as its own measure word.
No measure word: 一年, 两年. 年 works as its own measure word.
